fields.meta_title: Interactive Landing Page Builder With Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an interactive landing page with a calculator, quiz, configurator, or product tour that saves every visitor input with the lead.
fields.h1: Build an Interactive Landing Page That Answers Each Visitor
fields.hero_description: Get an interactive landing page with a calculator or quiz that shows results on the spot and saves each answer with the lead.
fields.features_heading: Controls That Hand the Visitor an Answer
fields.features_subheading: An interactive landing page asks for an input and shows a result on the same screen. Six parts turn that into a lead.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the control, get the page

Tell Emergent what the visitor enters and what the page shows back. It builds the page with that calculator or quiz working, and you change a formula later by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
The result appears beside the inputs

Ask for the answer to update next to the fields as the visitor types. A visitor who has seen their price has a reason to leave an email, which is why the form goes after it.
fields.feature_3:
Each answer stays with its lead

Every input is saved in the same row as the email it came with, in a database you own. Sales opens a lead and sees the square footage or quiz answers before the first call.
fields.feature_4:
Rates live in a table, not in the code

Keep prices and quiz outcomes in a table the page reads on each load. When the per-visit rate goes up, you edit one row in that table instead of hunting through a formula.
fields.feature_5:
Answers arrive in your CRM

Connect the page to HubSpot or another tool with an API, and each lead syncs there with its answers. A quiz result becomes a field on the contact, not a note typed in later.
fields.feature_6:
Every control works without a mouse

Ask for a visible label on each input and a number keypad on numeric fields. Before launch, tab through the page and move every slider and option with the keyboard alone.

fields.tab_content_1:
A $1,440 monthly quote with no sales call

Tellbrook Cleaning quotes offices by size and visit count. An office manager enters 4,000 square feet and 12 visits a month, and the calculator prices the space at $120 a visit and shows $1,440 a month. When the manager requests the quote, it is saved with both inputs, and Tellbrook's callback starts from that number.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four questions, then a roast to try

Kettlebay Roasters sells 3 roasts and uses 4 questions about brewing and taste to choose between them. The result screen recommends Dusk Ridge and says which answers led there. Only then does the email field appear, and the 4 answers are saved with the signup.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every pick lands in a $730 total

A buyer on Ormsby Desk Co's page picks a 60-inch top for $640 and a black frame for $90. The preview redraws after each pick, and the total reads $730 before the order form. The finished build is saved with the order, top and frame included.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which hotspot drew 64 of 180 visitors? Approvals

Quillstack sells expense software to agencies. Its page puts 4 clickable hotspots on a screenshot of the dashboard, and each one opens a short note on that feature. Of the 180 visitors who opened the tour this week, 64 clicked the approvals hotspot. The demo form sits after the last hotspot.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Interactive Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an interactive landing page that shows each visitor a correct result first and saves what they entered.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one answer the visitor wants
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the formula before you prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the email field after the result
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name what a visitor comes to the page to find out: a monthly price, or which product fits. Build one control around that answer. A page with a calculator and a quiz side by side splits attention between the two.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the inputs, the rates and the math on one line, such as square feet times $0.03 times visits a month. For a quiz, write which answers lead to which result. Anything you leave out, the build has to guess.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Paste that line into your prompt along with the fields you need and where the result should appear. Emergent builds the page with the control working, and you ask for changes in plain words until it matches your math.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Let the visitor see the price or the match before you ask for anything. Then offer the next step in that same view, with a button that names it, such as Request this quote.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Enter 5 sets of inputs you have already worked out by hand, including the smallest and largest you expect. Every result on the page should match yours to the cent before a visitor sees it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tab through it, then try it on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Reach every field, slider, and button with the Tab key and operate each one without a mouse. Then open the page on a phone and check that number fields bring up the number keypad.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the inputs your leads chose
fields.howto_step_7_des: After launch, sort the saved leads by what they entered. The office sizes people price and the quiz answers they give tell you which offer to put first on the next version of the page.

faq_plan.q: What is an interactive landing page?
faq_plan.a: An interactive landing page is a single-goal page where the visitor operates something, such as a price calculator or a product quiz, and gets a result back on the same screen. What they enter is saved with their contact details, which tells sales what each prospect asked about.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an interactive landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write down the inputs, the formula or quiz logic, and where the result appears. Then describe that to Emergent's AI landing page builder, which builds it with the calculator or quiz included. Check several results against your own math and tab through every field before you publish.

faq_plan.q: What do good interactive landing page examples ask visitors to do?
faq_plan.a: They ask for something the visitor can answer without looking it up, such as an office size or how they brew coffee, and they return a result at once. When you study an example, count its inputs and note whether the result comes before the form or after it.

faq_plan.q: Is an interactive landing page the same as an animated one?
faq_plan.a: No. An interactive page changes because the visitor did something, such as typing a number or picking an answer. An animated landing page moves on its own as it loads or scrolls. One page can do both, and a quiz with no motion at all is still interactive.

faq_plan.q: Should an interactive landing page show the result before asking for an email?
faq_plan.a: Yes, show the result first. Once visitors know the number, an email field reads as a way to keep it; placed in front of the answer, it asks for trust before the number has proven useful. Put the form directly under the result, with the inputs carried over.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a quiz on an interactive landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Start with 4, and add a question only when it changes the result. If every answer to a question leads to the same recommendation, cut it. Show progress, such as question 2 of 4, and when the quiz needs another question later, add it by prompting Emergent again.

faq_plan.q: Can a printed flyer link to an interactive landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Point a QR code at the page URL, and the visitor lands on the calculator or quiz with nothing to type. Because the scan happens on a phone, treat the page as a qr code landing page: one control that fits the screen and a button large enough for a thumb.

faq_plan.q: How do I make an interactive landing page work with a keyboard?
faq_plan.a: Use real form controls for every input and test the page with the Tab key. WCAG 2.1.1 asks that all functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface. Put the result in an output element: MDN notes that assistive technology will announce the results of UI interactions posted inside it without requiring that focus is switched away from the controls.

faq_plan.q: What should an interactive landing page save from each visitor?
faq_plan.a: Save every input next to the contact details, plus the result the page showed. A lead that reads 4,000 square feet, 12 visits, and $1,440 a month tells sales the quote before the first call. In the app Emergent builds, that data lives in a database the business owns and can sync to any tool with an API.

faq_plan.q: Do the sliders on an interactive landing page work on a phone?
faq_plan.a: They can, if each one is sized for a thumb and paired with a number field for an exact value. Set that field's inputmode attribute to numeric, which MDN describes as a numeric input keyboard that only requires the digits. Then test on a real phone: on a mobile landing page, keep the result on the same screen as the inputs.

plan.angle: The SERP for interactive landing page mixes definitions, inspiration galleries and motion tutorials, and blurs interactive with animated. This page holds one line: an interactive landing page is one the visitor operates (a calculator, a quiz, a configurator, a clickable tour) and every input they give is saved with the lead. It shows four such pages with the inputs and outputs drawn out, and gives the build rules the galleries skip: show the result before asking for an email, keep prices and rules in a table you can edit, label every field, and make every control work from a keyboard and a phone keypad. Motion belongs to the animated sibling and stays out of the headings.
